scope.sampling_criterion: All .tsx/.ts/.css under apps/portfolio/src, apps/blog/src, packages/ui/src, packages/config-tailwind (102 non-test files) read or grepped. Started from ground-truth in .audit/tools/playwright-portfolio.json and .audit/tools/playwright-blog.json (26 unique non-flaky axe failures across 2x-repeated full e2e runs), plus .audit/tools/eslint-portfolio.json and .audit/tools/eslint-blog.json (0 jsx-a11y messages in either, confirmed by direct query of all ruleIds). No standalone .audit/tools/axe.json or .audit/tools/eslint.json existed in this repo at run time; the per-app eslint-*.json and playwright-*.json (whose JSON reporter output embeds full axe violation payloads per failed test) were used instead. Beyond the given axe/eslint evidence, empirically verified via Playwright (playwright-core 1.61.1, driven directly since no MCP server is available) against production builds (pnpm build:portfolio, pnpm build:blog) served on localhost:4173/4174: full keyboard Tab walks on portfolio home and blog index (no trap/loss beyond expected end-of-document wrap), mobile hamburger overlay open/Tab-trap/Escape/focus-return cycle, and a DOM-wide interactive-element bounding-box sweep (24x24 CSS px check) on both apps' primary route at 375x812 in both themes. Landmarks (main/nav/footer/header) confirmed present via DOM query on both apps. No <form>/<input>/<textarea>/<select> exists anywhere in either app (Contact.tsx is link-only), so the Forms checklist item has no applicable surface. Not independently re-crawled: /resume, /projects (portfolio) beyond their axe pass/fail status, and blog post/ADR detail pages beyond the given axe results — treat coverage as route-representative, not exhaustive of every interactive element on every route.
tools_used: axe (via @axe-core/playwright, embedded in playwright JSON reporter output)

findings.title: Light-theme active nav-link text fails color-contrast (4.41:1 vs required 4.5:1) on every route in both apps

references: .audit/tools/playwright-portfolio.json (24 failing results, e.g. '/about has no automatically detectable accessibility violations (light, en) | chromium')
.audit/tools/playwright-blog.json (28 failing results, e.g. '/blog has no automatically detectable accessibility violations (light, en) | chromium')
apps/portfolio/src/components/Navbar.tsx:74 (active link: border-b-2 border-primary pb-1 font-bold text-primary)
evidence.tool_output: axe color-contrast, impact: serious. Element has insufficient color contrast of 4.41 (foreground color: #2d7670, background color: #e7eaed, font size: 12.0pt (16px), font weight: bold). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1, on <a class="border-b-2 border-primary pb-1 font-bold text-primary">. #e7eaed is not a token in theme.css; it is the composited color of --color-surface-container (#e3e6e9) at 80% opacity over --color-background (#f7f9fb) under backdrop-blur-md (verified by manual sRGB blend: 0.8*(227,230,233)+0.2*(247,249,251) = (231,234,237) = #e7eaed). This is why it isn't caught by checking theme.css's flat token values alone.

findings.impact: Every visitor in light mode (the OS-default theme for a large share of users, and reachable via the theme toggle from dark) sees the active/current-page nav indicator at 4.41:1, under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for 16px bold text. Fails automated CI gates identically on every axe-scanned route in both apps (portfolio: /, /about, /contact; blog: all 6 scanned routes) whenever that route's own nav item is the active one -- this is a systemic regression in the shared design token, not a per-page bug, and it is exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md's Testing section says should already be caught (axe checks across every route, in both light and dark themes).
findings.correction: Either lighten packages/config-tailwind/theme.css's :root.light --color-primary (#2d7670) enough to clear 4.5:1 against the composited ~#e7eaed navbar background, or remove/reduce the translucency on the navbar's bg-surface-container/80 (packages/ui/src/Navbar.tsx:103) so the active link renders against an opaque, higher-contrast surface. A token change must be re-verified against every other light-theme use of --color-primary (buttons, links, focus ring, prose links) per CLAUDE.md's 'Change a design token' recipe, not just the navbar.
findings.verification: Re-run pnpm --filter portfolio exec playwright test accessibility.spec.ts and pnpm --filter blog exec playwright test accessibility.spec.ts; all light-theme color-contrast failures should clear. Also spot-check the new --color-primary value doesn't regress the CTA/prose-link contrast elsewhere in :root.light.

findings.title: Collapsed timeline detail panels leave their links keyboard-focusable while aria-hidden="true" (aria-hidden-focus), on every theme/locale/viewport of the homepage

references: .audit/tools/playwright-portfolio.json (12 failing results for route '/', all 4 colorScheme x locale combinations x 3 projects, e.g. '/ has no automatically detectable accessibility violations (dark, en) | chromium')
apps/portfolio/src/components/TimelineItem.tsx:158-171 (div id={detailsId} aria-hidden={!expanded}, always mounted for the collapse/expand transition)
apps/portfolio/src/components/TimelineItem.tsx:197-212 (nested <a href={link.href}> with no tabIndex management tied to `expanded`)
evidence.tool_output:
axe aria-hidden-focus, impact: serious, tags include wcag2a/wcag412. Focusable content should have tabindex="-1" or be removed from the DOM, on
, related node Invest-MT. Confirmed present for two distinct milestones' panels (id="sedec-details" and id="shellhub-details") in the same scan, i.e. it is the general pattern for every milestone with a `links` field, not a one-off.

findings.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard users tabbing through the homepage timeline land on links that are visually and semantically hidden (opacity: 0, aria-hidden="true") whenever a milestone's detail panel is collapsed -- the default state. This is disorienting (focus appears to vanish, or an AT announces a hidden link's presence inconsistently with its aria-hidden ancestor) and affects both themes, both locales, and both desktop and mobile viewports, since it's driven by component state, not styling.
findings.correction: When `expanded` is false, either add tabIndex={-1} (and restore tabIndex={0}/remove the attribute when expanded) to every focusable descendant inside the detailsId panel (the technologies/links list), or set the native `inert` attribute on the panel while collapsed the same way packages/ui/src/Navbar.tsx already does for its own hidden overlay (the overlayRef.current?.toggleAttribute("inert", !isOpen) pattern) -- inert also stops it from being found by find-in-page/AT virtual cursor, which plain tabIndex=-1 doesn't.
findings.verification: Re-run pnpm --filter portfolio exec playwright test accessibility.spec.ts -g "/ has"; the aria-hidden-focus/focusable-not-tabbable violations should clear in all colorScheme x locale combinations. Manually Tab through a collapsed milestone card and confirm focus skips its (still-hidden) links entirely.

findings.title: Timeline 'Detalhes' toggle and 'Mostrar tudo' buttons render under the 24x24 CSS px minimum touch target

references: apps/portfolio/src/components/TimelineItem.tsx:141-150 (button, className has no padding utility: mt-2 flex items-center gap-1 font-label-mono text-label-mono uppercase tracking-widest text-primary)
apps/portfolio/src/components/Timeline.tsx:134-142 (button, className mt-4 font-label-mono text-label-mono uppercase tracking-widest text-primary, also no padding)
evidence.tool_output: Playwright DOM sweep (getBoundingClientRect) against the production build at 375x812, both themes, portfolio home: BUTTON Detalhes, w=89 h=21 (x3 occurrences, one per milestone with expandable content) and BUTTON Mostrar tudo (mais 14), w=207 h=21. Both are 21px tall, under the 24px CSS px minimum; identical in light and dark since sizing is theme-independent.

findings.impact: These are standalone tap controls (not inline text links, so the WCAG 2.5.8 'target in a sentence' exception does not apply) at 21px tall -- under the 24px minimum, they are a real mis-tap risk for touch and low-precision-pointer users, on every milestone card that has expandable content, and on the mobile 'show more' affordance that gates most of the timeline's content below the fold.
findings.correction: Add vertical padding (e.g. py-1 or py-1.5, matching the padding already used on LanguageSwitcher's buttons in packages/ui/src/LanguageSwitcher.tsx:45-46) to both buttons so their rendered height reaches >=24px, or wrap the text in a min-h-6 container.
findings.verification: Re-measure both buttons' getBoundingClientRect().height after the padding change; confirm >=24px at the same 375x812 viewport in both themes.

findings.title: Blog's empty tag-filter result message isn't announced to assistive tech (no live region)

references: apps/blog/src/components/ContentIndex.tsx:156 (activeTag state, set via TagChip onClick with no navigation)

findings.impact: Clicking a tag chip filters the blog/ADR index client-side (no route change). If the chosen tag yields zero entries, the only feedback is a plain paragraph appearing in the DOM -- a screen-reader user who isn't visually scanning the page gets no announcement that their filter action produced an empty result, and may assume the click did nothing.
findings.correction:
Wrap the empty-state message in a live region, e.g. add role="status" (or aria-live="polite") to the

at ContentIndex.tsx:201, matching the pattern already used in apps/blog/src/components/mdx/Pre.tsx:29 for its own aria-live usage.
findings.verification: With a screen reader (or by asserting the DOM attribute in a component test), click a tag with zero matching entries and confirm the empty-state text is announced without requiring the user to navigate to it.

findings.title: Timeline detail-panel technology/external links render under 24x24 CSS px

references: apps/portfolio/src/components/TimelineItem.tsx:197-212 (ul className="mt-2 flex flex-wrap gap-4" containing li > a href={link.href} className="font-body-md text-body-md text-primary underline")
evidence.tool_output: Playwright DOM sweep at 375x812, both themes: A Invest-MT, w=75 h=20 and A shellhub.io, w=81 h=20 -- both 20px tall.

findings.impact: These external links (rendered once a detail panel is expanded) are presented as short standalone list items rather than running text, so WCAG 2.5.8's inline-text exception is arguable but not clearly applicable; at 20px tall they sit under the 24px minimum. Lower severity than A11Y-003 because these only become visible/interactive after the user has already expanded a panel, and confidence is capped because the inline-text exception's applicability to short chip-style list links is a judgment call, not a clear-cut miss.
findings.correction: Give each li/a enough padding or line-height to reach a 24px hit area, consistent with the fix suggested for A11Y-003.
findings.verification: Re-measure link height after the change at the same viewport/theme combinations.

unverified_hypotheses.description: The same --color-primary/translucent-surface contrast pattern (A11Y-001) may also under-shoot 4.5:1 in other light-theme surfaces that combine text-primary with a semi-transparent background (e.g. Contact.tsx's bg-surface/60 cards, CardProjects.tsx's group-hover states) -- axe only flagged the nav because it's the only such combination present on every scanned route's initial render.
unverified_hypotheses.why_unverified: Would require enumerating every bg-*/NN + text-primary combination across both apps and computing each one's actual composited color, which wasn't done exhaustively; only the flagged navbar instance was traced to source.

unverified_hypotheses.description: apps/portfolio's /resume and /projects routes (scanned by accessibility.spec.ts but not in the given failing list) may still have light-theme contrast issues on elements axe's viewport/timing didn't happen to sample, or on interactive states (hover/focus) axe doesn't exercise.
unverified_hypotheses.why_unverified: Not independently re-scanned in this pass; relied on the provided playwright-portfolio.json's pass/fail status for those two routes.

unverified_hypotheses.description: The <a> elements behind the open_in_new icons on Contact.tsx (GitHub/LinkedIn/WhatsApp, all target="_blank") give no accessible indication that they open a new tab/window.
unverified_hypotheses.why_unverified: Not a WCAG 2.2 AA success-criterion violation (SC 3.2.5 Change on Request is AAA), so not filed as a finding, but noted as a UX/best-practice gap worth a follow-up outside this audit's Critical/High/Medium bar.
